description.narrative: The development objective of the project is to increase access to improved urban infrastructure services in selected medium-sized cities in Vietnam.

The objective of the Medium Cities Development Project for Vietnam is to increase access to improved urban infrastructure services in Lao Cai City, Phu Ly City, and Vinh City in a sustainable and efficient manner. There are four components to the project, the first component being urban basic infrastructure upgrading and service improvement. This component will improve urban infrastructure and service conditions in existing or newly developed urban areas and resettlement areas, including construction and rehabilitation of basic infrastructure systems such as water supply and sanitation, drainage, power supply, lighting, roads, and schools. The second component is the urban water supply and environmental sanitation. This component will construct and rehabilitee of primary and secondary infrastructure for water supply, drainage, wastewater collection and treatment, and flood mitigation, including improving drainage and pavement of roads. The third component is the urban roads and bridges: construction of roads and bridges. Finally, the fourth component is the project management support and technical assistance.

title.narrative: Length of waste water pipeline laid

comment.narrative: <p>Target substantially achieved (94%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 47.9 km wastewater pipelines laid and put into service in wards across the city; Phu Ly City: 30.13 km wastewater pipelines laid and put into service in wards across the city; Vinh City: 24 km wastewater pipelines laid and put into service in wards across the city. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

title.narrative: Length of new or upgraded local road

comment.narrative: <p>Target exceeded (103%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 88.56 km by upgrading road surfaces for 89 internal roads in the old part of the city; upgrading road surfaces on both the right and left banks of the Red River; rehabilitating recreation road around the Lao Cai Central Lake; and constructing new asphalt roads in the Dong Ha and Soi Lan resettlement sites and the Van Hoa commune; Phu Ly City: 13.38 km by constructing roads in Quang Trung, Duong Am, and Quynh Chan low-income residential areas on top of wastewater drainage pipes constructed under the project; and traffic routes in Trieu Xa and Me Noi areas running along the Southern embankment of the Chau Giang River to connect with the bypass road DT.491; Vinh City: 18 km by constructing new roads within the Quan Bau Resettlement Site; new roads within the Nghi Phu Resettlement Site; and additional service roads adjacent to Bac Channel, around the regulation lake, and around Vinh Citadel. All roads were put into service. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

<p>Target achieved (100%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 38 classrooms built in three new schools in Dong Ha resettlement site, including a pre-school, a primary school, and a secondary school; Phu Ly City: 92 classrooms built in five new schools, including a kindergarten and primary school in Quang Trung, a secondary school in Luong Khanh, a kindergarten in Phu Van, and a primary school in Tran Quoc. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

<p>Target exceeded (105%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 97.75 km non-rural roads constructed and put into service; Phu Ly City: 22.2 km non-rural roads constructed and put into service; Vinh City: 32.5 km non-rural roads constructed and put into service. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

title.narrative: Degree of citizen engagement - Beneficiaries involved in consultation of planning/ implementation/ evaluation of project.

comment.narrative: <p>Target substantially achieved (93%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 76,250 beneficiaries (of whom 50.0% were female); Phu Ly City: 29,038 beneficiaries (of whom 51.40% were female); Vinh City: 125,000 beneficiaries (of wom 51.10% were female).  The result reflects the number of city residents who engaged in consultations on the planning, implementation, and evaluation of the project. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

title.narrative: Number of people in urban areas provided with access to Improved Sanitation under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Target exceeded (126%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 59,868 people (of whom 50% were female); Phu Ly City: 58,119 people (of whom 50.8% were female); Vinh City: 162,593 people (of whom 51.07% were female). These peoplegained access to improved sanitation thanks to project investments which included the following: in Lao Cai City the construction of a new wastewater treatment plant, new pumping stations, sewer pipes and roadside drainage system, as well as the rehabilitation ofLao Cai central regulation lake; in Phu Ly City, the construction of a new wastewater treatment station, new sewers and clean waterpipes, and two pumping stations to transfer wastewater. In Vinh City the moat around the Citadel was rehabilitated, along with other bodies of water, drainage channels were constructed, and the city’s main wastewater pumping station saw its capacity almost double (from 12,600 to 25,000 m3/day). This total also includes the pupils and the teachers at the schools in Vinh and Lao Cai whichsaw their sanitation facilities (mainly toilets and handwashing facilities). Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

title.narrative: Implementation of a comprehensive and sustainable urban asset management plan with an approved annual budget for adequate O&M

comment.narrative: <p>Target partially achieved. Three plans were implemented—one in each city. In each of the three cities, an asset management system was established with a server located within the Urban Management Department. Since the completion of this activity, funds hve been allocated annually for O&M in each of the three cities, including for the infrastructure financed under the project. However, in both Lao Cai City and Vinh City, the budgets have been insufficient to adequately cover O&M costs. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

title.narrative: Length of primary roads and bridges constructed or improved

comment.narrative: <p>Target exceeded (118%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 10.21 km by constructing the new D1 road (now called Vo Nguyen Giap Street); and the Ngoi Dum 1 and Ngoi Dum 2 bridges; Phu Ly City: 9.75 km by constructing by constructing the new D4-N7 route, including four lanes with pedestrian crossings, drainage system, trees, and streetlights; Bien Hoa Road, which is the main road of Phu Ly City; and primary roads surrounding the Lam Ha and Quang Trung conditioning reservoirs; Vinh City: 14.6 km by constructing the four-lane Hung Tay-Vinh Road (including Ke Gai Bridge), and the two-lane road connecting NH46 to Lam Riverside Road. All roads were put into service. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

title.narrative: Reduction in vehicle operating time on new roads

comment.narrative:
<p>Target exceeded (117%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 30% reduction, Phu Ly City: 35% reduction, Vinh City: 40% reduction. The reduction is thanks to project investments in new and upgraded roads and bridges, namely the major Vo Nguyen Giap road and many local roads in Lao Cai City; route D4-N7 and Bien Hoa Road in Phu Ly City, and the four-lane Hung Tay-Vinh Road and the two-lane road between the N46 and Lam riverside in Vinh City (both roads included bridges). The result was calculated by comparing measured, actual journey times on routes before the investments were started and after they were completed at the same time of day. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: School students provided with access to newly built or improved classrooms

comment.narrative: <p>Target exceeded (126%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 1,208 students (of whom 46% were female); Phu Ly City: 3,113 students (of whom 48% were female). Improved access to newly built or improved classrooms was achieved in Lao Cai City through the construction of a pre-school, primary school, and secondary school in Dong Ha Resettlement Site. In Phu Ly City, it was achieved through the construction of five schools, including a kindergarten and primary school in Quang Trung, a secondary school in Luong Khanh, a kindergarten in Phu Van, and a primary school in Tran Quoc Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

<p>Target exceeded (171%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 109,920 beneficiaries (of whom 50.0% were female); Phu Ly City: 69,056 beneficiaries (of whom 50.80% were female); Vinh City: 333,764 beneficiaries (of whom 51.10% were female). The result reflects people living within project wards where investments took place. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

title.narrative: Number of schools with completed sanitation facilities

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved (100%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 27 schools equipped with functioning toilets and hand-washing systems; Vinh City: 27 schools equipped with functioning toilets and hand-washing systems. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

title.narrative: Additional wastewater treatment capacity made available

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved (100%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 4,300 m3/day by constructing the first wastewater treatment plant in Lao Cai City; Phu Ly City: 1,500 m3/day by constructing the Chau Giang wastewater treatment plant. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs. </p>

title.narrative: Number of people in urban areas provided with access to Improved Water Sources under the project

comment.narrative: <p>Target exceeded (147%). The result reflects the number of people with access in Lao Cai City. The result was achieved due to the capacity added to the Coc San Water Plant and the distribution pipes for the additional water supply, enabling residents to have better access to clean water. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

title.narrative: Additional treated water supply capacity made available

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved (100%). The result reflects the expanded water supply capacity in Lao Cai City by expanding the capacity of the Coc San Water Treatment Plant from 18, 000m3/day to 24,000m3/day. The result reflects the cumulative additional daily treated water supply to the water supply network. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

title.narrative: Length of water supply pipeline laid

comment.narrative: <p>Target substantially achieved (99%). The result reflects the following city-specific results: Lao Cai City: 57.7 km water supplypipelines laid and put into service, expanding the city's water supply network to all wards and communes compared to only partial coverage before the project; Phu Ly City: 20.2 km water supply pipelines laid and put into service in Quang Trung Ward, Hoa Lac Village (Lam Ha Commune), and Me Noi Village (Liem Chinh Commune); Vinh City: 10.3 km water supply pipelines laid and put into service in Quan Bau and Nghi Phu resettlement sites. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>

title.narrative: Length of drainage channel constructed or rehabilitated (including interceptors)

comment.narrative: <p>Target achieved (100%). The result reflects a 9.8 km open channel covered at the end of Bac Channel in Vinh City and put into service. Information source: PMU reports, review of supporting consultants’ completion report, discussion with PMUs.</p>
